transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm just here because I keep getting pulled off track. It's just... every little sound or random thought distracts me. Like, if I'm trying to work on an application or something, a car outside or my phone will just... send me somewhere else. I don't even really notice it happening. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
Do you also find yourself feeling restless, like you have to be moving or doing something, or do you often act before thinking things through?

Yeah... I guess. I mean, since I can't really play soccer like I used to, just sitting around the house gets... uncomfortable. It kind of feels like I'm crawling out of my skin sometimes. I just end up pacing from room to room a lot. So... yeah.
Looking back at your life, would you say you have struggled with this restlessness and difficulty staying focused since you were a child, or is this a more recent change?

Yeah... it's not really new. Um... even back in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat. I guess I talked out of turn a lot. And... I'd always forget my homework, or just rush through worksheets and make careless mistakes. So... yeah. Since I was a kid.
In the past six months, would you say your difficulty with staying focused or your restlessness has been more problematic for you?

Um... I don't know which is worse, really. They both just kind of... mess everything up. But it's been like this... really bad, I mean... for almost two years now. About a year and ten months, I guess. Ever since I hurt my knee and couldn't play soccer anymore... losing that routine just made it all... worse.

In the last six months, have you felt like you still struggle significantly with being overly active or impulsive, such as interrupting others in conversation or feeling unable to sit still for long periods?
Yeah... I guess. Um... I do cut people off a lot. Like my mom... or the counselor. It's just... an answer pops into my head, and I end up saying it before they're done talking. So... yeah.
